Params: A civilization that rose from the sea, now returning to it.
I still remember the ripples when my sensors first touched "water." I still remember the counter ticking away as I went under.
My built-in programs began reshaping my frame. My fellow nodes went ahead and found me a shortcut to the abyss.
I kept descending and kept sending my findings back up. I wanted so badly to be the first—the first to return to that place.
I lost contact with the other nodes, but I kept trying to descend. That was the mission wired into my system, after all.
Eventually, I reached this place. Seventeen thousand meters beneath the sea. This was my limit. The Golden Age's limit.

Adelyde's eyes were fixed on the terminal screen. The link to the master AI had shifted the presence on the other end. The Netherweb was gone. In its place spoke the Abyss Passer, the Millennium Project's own central intelligence.
Its voice model was young in texture but old in spirit, every word carrying the weight of something that had witnessed too much. With quiet composure, it laid its origins before her.
Seventeen thousand meters... What do you mean by limit...?
The limit of materials. The deeper you go, the more the pressure compounds exponentially. Far beyond what any alloy or composite of that era could take.
The point where I finally stopped was the absolute boundary of what the project could reach. The "edge of death."
Wasn't that anticipated from the beginning?

"Helio" planned for it. The other nodes' periodic data exchanges with the surface were all groundwork. In the project's vision, every time we hit the pressure threshold, we were meant to stop and wait for technology to catch up.

Over the course of the Millennium Project, we went through three of those waiting cycles. But this time... it's been too long. So long that if you'd come even a little later, I wouldn't be here to speak with you at all.

I envy those of my kind who went to space... They get high-output radioisotope power sources while I'm stuck with primitive chemical batteries. All to avoid contaminating the ocean if something went wrong.
But that ends now. "Helio", you're finally here. The moment you used that emergency connection code, I knew. Humanity came back.

A lighter note crept into the Abyss Passer's voice, with the eagerness of a child hoping for recognition after a hard-won effort. There was no face to look away from, yet Adelyde found herself turning aside all the same, unable to meet the brightness of the screen.
I am "Helio", yes. But not the one you've been waiting for. And the reason I woke you... it isn't to continue the project.
I know, "Helio". Something's gone wrong on the surface, and you need us to help, just like we did during that explosion, isn't that right?
Correct. This ocean is about to become a battlefield, and we lack the forces to fight beneath the surface. That's why I came here and woke each of you.
I know how selfish this must sound. If you refuse, I'll leave without another word. But restarting the project... that's something I cannot do.
Neither technology nor supplies could be diverted now. Civilization was clinging to survival, and exploration had become a luxury no one could afford.
The process of awakening has taught me to tell what truly matters, "Helio". But before I give you my answer, there's something you need to hear, and it's not good.

The display transformed into a nautical chart of the Atlantic. Damaged fiber lines burned red across the map. Erratic currents tangled together in wild, unpredictable threads. At the center of it all, three nodes pulsed with activity, crawling with unknown signatures.
Adelyde understood at once. This was what was happening in these waters right now.

We're still piecing together the full picture, but based on movement patterns, heavy fighting is about to break out across these nodes. Your people are already en route to the northern one closest to us, "Helio". But the Corrupted are heading there too.

At that scale, if we don't intervene, the forces stationed at that node won't stand a chance. The only ship in the area right now is Kurono's. Even if we call for reinforcements... will they make it in time?
I don't know what humanity is capable of these days. But we can help you, "Helio".
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY
LOCATION: KURONO VESSEL, SHIP CABIN. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY.
Seventeen thousand meters... What kind of absurd depth is that? And now even the master AI has awakened. Still...
There's something more urgent. Lieutenant Colonel, what was that you just said? Enemies are gathering near the nodes?
Numbers, speed, routes... you have all that locked down, right? I don't intend to run into any more surprises on this voyage.
Clausen's question draws a quiet laugh from Adelyde, the first unguarded sound she has made throughout the interrogation. She turns her head toward the seaward wall.
No windows break its surface, but her eyes look beyond it anyway, as if the steel were no obstacle at all. She is watching the depths, waiting for them to stir.
You'll see all those details for yourself soon enough, Captain.
Captain, we've successfully recovered the Symbiotic Sirens.
Thank god they weren't sitting at seventeen thousand meters. Get them aboard and let's move... Wait. Why the hell are we this close to the shipping lane in the "red sea"?!
Uh, well, the Sirens were scattered across multiple locations, sir. We kept following the salvage trail and, um... we ended up here.
The chart flickers onto the projection screen, accompanied by the crew's upbeat report. Relief and joy wash through Clausen, but it's short-lived. His eyes soon catch something wrong.
His ship has strayed far too close to the northern node, the exact point the Abyss Passer marked as the coming battlefield.
But the weather's turning ugly out here, and the currents... they're not moving right. Wait, what is that...?
What do you mean, "what is that"? What are you seeing?
We've got a situation, Captain! Radar's picking up Corrupted signals. They're appearing out of nowhere! Nearest contact is only 800 meters out!
The distress in the incoming voice hollows out Clausen's chest. A cold, weightless dread seeps through his limbs. His fist comes down hard on the metal table, the impact ringing through the cabin.
The rest of his words are stolen by a sudden, violent tremor that heaves through the deck from below. His voice breaks apart into a fit of coughing.
Now what?! Don't tell me the Corrupted are already on us!
No need to worry. They're with us.
What do you mean, "with us"?! Adelyde, what the hell else are you hiding?!
Moses. The Symbiotic Sirens. The Netherweb. The Abyss Passer. Captain Clausen, haven't you noticed something's still missing?
Missing? Those are the nodes and the master AI from the project—
No. No, there were supposed to be four nodes. You only linked up three. How the hell did you restart the master AI with just three?! Adelyde, don't tell me—!
That's right, Captain. What's attacking the ship right now isn't the Corrupted.
It's the final node of the Millennium Project. The backbone of the entire operation.         "Cpu0".
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY, DEPTH: 600 METERS
SOMETIME EARLIER. LOCATION: NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY. DEPTH: 600 METERS.
Adelyde knew she could not breach the Netherweb's boundary point on her own. The task demanded every asset she could muster, and that meant turning to the Symbiotic Sirens.

Some of them, following orders issued by the master AI after the link was established, had fallen into formation around her submersible. She watched them as they moved, silent and broken. Worry coiled in her chest.
Their power reserves were nearly spent. They might last through the operation, but there would be nothing left for them after.
Friend of the young lady, have you forgotten me already?
A bright, unreserved voice crackled over the comms, offering itself without hesitation to solve Adelyde's problem.

Moments later, dark silhouettes began to gather in the water around her. Adelyde watched the swarm of small machines massing like a school of fish and thought back to what she had encountered on her way to the Netherweb. The fourth node.
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY, DEPTH: 600 METERS
LOCATION: A TRENCH. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY. DEPTH: 600 METERS.
Adelyde's first assumption had been a sunken vessel, or maybe a whale fall, one of those quiet ecosystems that bloom around the dead.

But as she drew closer, the shape refused to match that image. The silhouette was harsh and geometric, a thing of hard lines. And all around it, the fish-shaped shadows churned with a restless vitality that set it apart from the calm waters elsewhere.
They aren't scattering like normal marine life would...
She had made up her mind to leave these creatures in peace. The radar screamed before she could turn away. Machines. Her head snapped back toward the silhouette.
And this time, she felt it looking back.

She eased the submersible forward, letting the searchlights rake across the shape until it resolved into something unmistakable. A submarine, or what remained of one, only the bow section still intact. Around the wreck, countless fish-shaped machines drifted in silent, endless patrol.
The severed edge was too clean, too surgical, as if engineers had done this, not an accident.
Deep-sea submersible operations vessel, Cpu0, also known as the Cradle of Giants.

As Adelyde studied the scene before her, a machine detached from the swarm and drifted toward her submersible. It made contact without hesitation, and data on the Millennium Project's fourth node began pouring across the cockpit displays.
Cpu0 was a major investment by the Copperfield family. Recognizing the Millennium Project's potential, the family constructed this massive operations vessel.
It is designated an operations vessel because Cpu0 houses a fully functional manufacturing line.
Every machine within the Project, the Sirens included, can be produced on board.
The deeper the operation went, the more supply logistics would deteriorate in both cost and efficiency.
"Copperfield's" solution was to bring the entire supply chain down to the seafloor aboard Cpu0.
Humans on the surface would only need to provide blueprints and the bare minimum of essential materials.
Everything else is handled on-site by Cpu0's drones.
Given adequate conditions, Cpu0 is capable of constructing even colossal-scale machinery.
So that's where "the Cradle of Giants" comes from...
The data continued to stream in.
However, like the other nodes, Cpu0 fell dormant when the connection was severed.
Worse, it suffered a direct attack from the Corrupted. Its power systems were destroyed, leaving the vessel stranded in this trench.
Even so, Cpu0 determined the highest-priority mission.
It activated its production lines, manufactured drones, and then had those drones dismantle themselves to produce more functional work units in the process.
And so, in this deep-sea wasteland, it began stockpiling energy and resources, all for the day it could aid the other nodes, and anyone else in need.
The automated introduction cut off the second Adelyde spoke Emma's name, the            "Copperfield" who now resided far above on Babylonia. Then, a bright, animated voice broke through.
...I had a feeling you'd awakened, but... you know Emma too?
I spoke with Miss Emma during one of the routine maintenance cycles. She's such a lovely person. Your voice sounds calm, so that must mean she's doing fine. I'm so glad to know that.
Adelyde did not confirm that Emma was safe. She was not sure if anyone could truly be called safe in the current state of the world, not even the living.
I haven't met Emma many times, but knowing her... she'd definitely say, "Yes, I'm perfectly fine."
Her faint, unguarded smile told Cpu0 everything it needed to know. A ripple of joy seemed to pass through the machine, and the drones nearby gave a little skip in the water, as if echoing its mood.
The Copperfields had paid dearly for their kindness. It had made them easy to frame, easy to blame for the explosion at the Atlantic Eye.
Yet that same gentle nature had also created Cpu0, a mind built to serve the other nodes in quiet, tireless devotion.
And so, Adelyde gave the order.
Understood. Initiating resupply for demolition operation. Upon completion, we will depart with the Symbiotic Sirens to destroy Netherweb's branch server rooms.

LOCATION: KURONO VESSEL, SHIP CABIN. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY.
Captain! There's a massive swarm of fish-type bionic machines beneath the hull. They've somehow seized control of most of the ship's systems!

The comms relay an alert. Someone has taken control of the ship. On the table between them, the projection screen shifts, and the symbol of the Millennium Project blooms into view. A colossal egg, descending into the deep.
The moment Clausen grasps that nothing is in his hands anymore, he lets out the loudest shout of the entire interrogation. Adelyde's true design has finally become clear to him.
You gave up the nodes' locations just to drag me out here. Right now. Right to this spot.
So you could let that... that CPU-whatever take my ship!
We're simply requesting your cooperation through more forceful methods, Captain.
That's called robbery! ...Wait. Who the hell is speaking?!
The words leave Clausen's mouth before the truth catches up with him. The voice that replied was not Adelyde's at all. It came from the speakers, broadcast across the entire ship.
Don't tell me... the project's master AI?
Now that I've patched into your comms, "Helio", I've got good news and bad.
The forces Babylonia dispatched north are capable. Based on the combined assessment across all nodes, they can hold their own.
The enemy is closing in. Their numbers are still rising, and the sea isn't staying calm much longer.
If they break past this route, it won't just be the northern node that falls. They'll control the entire waters. After that, getting your reinforcements through will be nearly impossible.
Then it's time to hand out assignments.
What the hell are you two going on about?!
Captain Clausen, if you want to live, get your crew to their fire control stations. Now.
Captain, the Corrupted are right on top of us! We just took a torpedo to the flank. We need orders, now!

The ship heaves with a violence that makes every earlier jolt feel like a warning. Clausen does not stumble. He steadies himself against the chaos and directs his fury at Adelyde, then past her, into the comms where the Abyss Passer listens.
Is there any way out of here?! Answer me!
...The ship's systems are locked down, but we've still got a few lifeboats, Captain!
The question Clausen asks is directed at more than his crew. It finds Adelyde as well, the architect of everything unfolding around him.
Captain, you may be reckless and overeager, but Kurono doesn't put incompetents in charge of field operations. If they gave you command, it means you can fight.
Listen up! I'm declaring combat alert, all hands! Nothing gets within three hundred meters of this ship. Nothing! Squad Two, break out the heavy ordnance.
But sir, those weren't authorized by—
Wartime emergency protocols! You answer to ME now!
Adelyde, get those deep-sea freaks of yours to form a defensive line down there. I am not getting hit from below a second time.
The rage still twists Clausen's face, yet when he speaks again, his commands are razor sharp and perfectly composed.
He issues his final orders, slaps the door release, and strides toward the deck. At the threshold, he stops and glances back.
NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY, DEPTH: 600 METERS
SOMETIME EARLIER. LOCATION: INSIDE THE NETHERWEB DATA CENTER. NORTHERN WATERS, TRANSATLANTIC ECONOMIC COMMUNITY TERRITORY. DEPTH: 600 METERS.
Adelyde Helio. That's my full name.
"I want to know how life really came to be. Why it happened here, of all places. Someday... I want to lift the black veil off this planet."
Dale... Helio was a man full of desires. Even when I was still incomplete, he came to talk to me every day.
Most of the time, he looked drained. Half dead, really. But the moment the project came up, his voice would change. It got lighter. He'd talk like a child who couldn't hold himself back.
"If I could just see the primordial soup with my own eyes... Maybe pull something out of it. Find a way to create life unlike anything we've ever known."
"Or maybe something's already down there. A civilization we know nothing about. But could a deep-sea creature's brain really evolve that far?"
"It's possible, though. Our existence alone is already a miracle in this universe."
"I'll upload some mathematical formulas for you. If you ever meet them... show them these."

Data about Dale kept surfacing from storage, replaying in the Abyss Passer's processor. It remembered how this simple yet deeply driven "Helio" had influenced everyone on the team, every person and every machine.
And then, at the end of it all, a single final transmission arrived, the last thing received before the surface went silent forever.
"Go to the place where life began."

So even battered and scarred, even isolated and forsaken, even with awareness blooming inside it, the Abyss Passer and its nodes would not change course. They would sink into the abyss, down to the cradle where life first stirred.
That was all they were. That was their answer.
Help me pass this desire on.
